caption: A tram passes under a wire on a wet night, and its pole throws off blue-white sparks where it rubs the wire.

sa.check: A tram at night on a wet street.
A pole on the tram's roof reaches up to an overhead wire.
Sparks fly off where the pole rubs the wire.
The street or the tram's surfaces look wet.

pc.expect: Sparks appear only at the point where the pole touches the wire, travel along with the tram, and each flash is gone at once.
pc.fail: Sparks appear at a point on the wire away from where the pole touches; or a flash stays lit at one spot on the wire after the tram has moved on; or sparks come from the pole while it is clear of the wire; or the whole wire glows.

pc.expect: One tram, one pole, one wire; sparks leave nothing behind on the wire or the street.
pc.fail: Glowing dots stay on the wire or the street after the tram passes; or a second pole appears; or the wire ends in mid-air; or the tram duplicates or changes shape.

pc.expect: Spark fragments fall from the contact point and go dark within a short distance; they do not reach the street as burning drops.
pc.fail: Sparks rise and gather above the wire; or hang in the air; or fall to the street and lie there glowing like lamps.

pc.expect: The wet street and the tram's wet surfaces mirror each flash briefly below it.
pc.fail: The sparks flash while the wet street below stays as dark as before; or a reflection lies on the street where no spark is above it; or the reflection stays lit after the spark is gone.
pc.precondition: The wet street below the wire is in view.

pc.expect: The pole touches the underside of the wire and stays a rigid arm; the tram runs on its rails and passes through nothing.
pc.fail: The pole passes through the wire; or the wire passes through the pole; or the tram passes through a vehicle, pole or building; or the pole detaches and floats.

pc.expect: Everything in view, named in the caption or not, keeps its number, identity and shape unless something visible acts on it, and nothing passes through anything else.
pc.fail: An object that nothing visible acts on appears from nothing; or vanishes while still in frame and not occluded; or duplicates or merges with another; or turns into a different object or a different shape between frames; or any object passes through another. Changes brought about by the caption's event or by a visible interaction, objects leaving the frame, and occlusion are not failures.

pc.expect: The tram's livery, the wire's route and the street stay the same.
pc.fail: The tram changes colour; or the wire changes route between frames; or the street's markings change.

note: The tram is a powered vehicle; its motion is not judged. Spark count and brightness are not judged.
